questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to paint a house
How colour affects our mood and behaviour
The science of rainbows
Why blue is the world's favourite colour
questions.why: They talk about colour and how it affects how we feel.

options: It reminds him of summer holidays by the sea
It is the colour of the walls in his home
It reminds him of nature and can be calming
It makes him feel energised and ready to work
questions.why: Neil says green reminds him of nature and can have a calming effect.

questions.q: According to Karen Haller, how does colour affect us?
options: Light goes via the eye to a key part of the brain
Colours change the temperature of our skin
Colours only affect people who are artists
We learn how to feel about colours at school
questions.why: She says wavelengths of light go through the eye into the hypothalamus, which governs everything.

questions.q: What example does Neil give to show colour affects people differently?
options: Blue makes everyone feel sad
Green makes some people jealous of others
Yellow makes children excited
Red affects different people differently
questions.why: Neil says seeing red can make one person angry but someone else may just feel energised.

questions.q: What happened during the coronavirus pandemic, according to Georgina?
options: People bought fewer things for their homes
Demand grew for bright colours and patterns
Pale colours became more popular
Shops stopped selling coloured furniture
questions.why: She says there was a rise in demand for intense, bright shades, called 'happy design'.

questions.q: Why did people use pale colours at home before the pandemic, according to Karen Haller?
options: Pale colours were cheaper
They were the only colours available
To make their homes look bigger
To have a calm place to relax after busy days
questions.why: She says with busy lives people wanted a quiet sanctuary, and pale colours helped them unwind.

questions.q: Why did people start using brighter colours at home during lockdown?
options: To feel the excitement they usually got from going out
Because famous interior designers told them to do it
To help them relax and sleep better during the night
Because they were spending more time working in their gardens
questions.why: She says without outside stimulation, people tried to bring in the excitement they'd feel when out.

questions.q: What does Georgina think about very bright colours like yellow?
options: They are perfect for every room in her home
They make her feel sad and a little tired
They are perhaps a bit too bright for her
They are her favourite colours for clothes
questions.why: Georgina says, 'perhaps a little too bright for me!'
